This drone can't crash, and that's mathematically proven.
MIT built a planner called SANDO. It flies through places with no map, while unknown things move around it.
Most planners only promise safety when obstacles stand still, or when the map is known.
SANDO's trick: it can't know where a moving object goes, but it knows its top speed.
So it wraps each object in a growing bubble, the farthest it could possibly travel.
Then it builds a safe corridor through space and time, around every bubble.
A heat map steers it away from crowded zones, and it replans on board, on the fly.
In simulation it reached goals faster than top systems, with zero collisions. In 12 real flights, it hit nothing.
Latoon. Voyaging the unseen. Follow for more.
